name: Floor Press
description: The floor press is a horizontal pressing exercise performed lying on the floor rather than on a bench. The floor limits the range of motion by stopping the elbows at the floor's surface, eliminating the deep pectoral stretch of the bench press and placing the emphasis on the lockout portion of the press. This makes it an excellent accessory lift for building triceps strength and training through joint-friendly range of motion.

execution.starting_position: Lie on the floor with knees bent and feet flat. Hold a barbell or dumbbells above the chest with arms extended. The barbell should be unracked from safeties or handed off by a partner.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the barbell in a rack or on safeties at a low height before lying under it, or have a partner hand it off after you are in position on the floor.
steps: Step 1: Lie on the floor with knees bent, feet flat. Unrack or accept the barbell above your chest.
Step 2: Inhale and lower the bar by bending the elbows until both upper arms rest on the floor.
Step 3: Pause momentarily with the upper arms resting on the floor — do not bounce.
Step 4: Exhale and press the bar back to the top with triceps emphasis.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on the descent; exhale on the press.
common_mistakes: Bouncing the elbows off the floor, which uses momentum rather than muscle
Flaring the elbows wide, which reduces tricep activation
safety_considerations: Without a rack, you need a training partner to hand off and receive the bar
Keep the lower back flat against the floor — avoid arching
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Lower until the upper arms touch the floor gently; press to full extension.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 2-1-2-0 (pause 1 second on the floor before pressing)
coaching_cues: Pause dead-stop before pressing — eliminate all momentum
Drive the bar up and slightly back toward the head during extension
